run.change_description: lib/batcher: prevent commits racing shutdown - fixes #9687

summary.intent: Close a shutdown race in lib/batcher: `Commit` could pass its closed-check and enqueue behind `Shutdown`'s quit marker, hanging a sync caller forever or silently dropping an async upload (issue rclone/rclone#9687, reproduced by `ncw`).
summary.issue_fit: Met — `admitMu` (batcher.go:50) now serializes `Shutdown`'s close(b.closed)+enqueue-quit (batcher.go:243-252) with `Commit`'s closed-check+enqueue (batcher.go:267-281), so every admitted commit is enqueued strictly before the quit marker and every commit arriving after shutdown observes the closed error; verified via two confirmed concurrency safety premises (see Verification).
summary.coverage: Both changed files (lib/batcher/batcher.go, lib/batcher/batcher_test.go) fully read at head against merge-base; the new `TestBatcherCommitRacingShutdown` traced line-by-line for both sync and async modes and confirmed it fails pre-fix (hang/drop) and passes post-fix by tracing the `fs.Debugf`/log-level gated blocking mechanism against fs/log.go. No other files touch lib/batcher's exported surface (backend/dropbox and backend/googlephotos are the only Batcher callers and are unchanged).
check_details: Reviewer ran `go test -count=1 -race ./lib/batcher/...` at head 0b87bc478: PASS (5.3s).
Reviewer ran `go test -count=20 -race -run TestBatcherCommitRacingShutdown ./lib/batcher/...` at head 0b87bc478: PASS (5.1s).
Reviewer ran `go vet ./lib/batcher/...` at head 0b87bc478: clean, no output.

PR body also claims `go build` and `PATH="$PWD:$PATH" make quicktest` passed; neither is reproducible in this offline sandbox (the dependency cache holds only lib/batcher and its test imports), and no captured output or CI run was supplied, so both are unavailable rather than accepted.

observations.fact: `Commit`'s admission critical section now spans its debug-log call and the send on `b.in`, so concurrent `Commit` calls (and `Shutdown`) fully serialize on `admitMu` for that duration instead of contending only on the channel; unmeasured, and the PR's own `-race -count=20` and this review's runs show no timeout regression.

requirements.evidence: lib/batcher/batcher.go:50 adds `admitMu sync.Mutex`; batcher.go:243-252 and batcher.go:267-281 hold it across Shutdown's close(b.closed)+enqueue-quit and Commit's closed-check+enqueue respectively, serializing admission with shutdown-marker insertion.
lib/batcher/batcher.go:270-271 still returns `fserrors.FatalError(errors.New("batcher is shutting down"))`, the same error type and text as before the change, for commits observed after shutdown.

lib/batcher/batcher_test.go:239-311 adds `TestBatcherCommitRacingShutdown`, table-driven over sync/async, using a `blockingStringer` to pause `Commit` mid-admission and assert neither a hang (sync) nor a silently dropped upload (async); reviewer traced and reproduced pass at head (see check_details) and traced why it would fail pre-fix.

Issue's closing question — whether admission and shutdown-marker insertion should be serialized so every accepted request is processed or explicitly rejected — is answered affirmatively by the same admitMu-guarded critical sections; independently confirmed by two verified concurrency safety premises (record.verification).

Reviewer reproduced the race-focused claim narrowly: `go test -count=1 -race ./lib/batcher/...` and `go test -count=20 -race -run TestBatcherCommitRacingShutdown ./lib/batcher/...` both pass at head; `go vet ./lib/batcher/...` is clean (check_details).

`go build` and `make quicktest` are claimed but not independently reproducible offline (dependency cache scoped to lib/batcher only; no readable CI output supplied); nothing in the diff suggests either would behave differently, and lib/batcher's exported surface (New/Commit/Shutdown/Batching signatures) is unchanged, so nothing material is judged to depend on this gap.

tasks.premise: b.admitMu makes Shutdown's close(b.closed)+enqueue-of-the-quit-request one atomic critical section with each Commit's closed-check+enqueue, so once Shutdown's critical section (batcher.go:243-252) has completed, no Commit call (batcher.go:266-281) can still observe b.closed open and enqueue its request into b.in behind the quit marker.

Holding admitMu across Commit's send on the buffered channel b.in cannot deadlock against Shutdown, because commitLoop runs in its own always-live goroutine that keeps receiving from b.in independently of admitMu until it reads the quit request, and Shutdown only enqueues that quit request (still under admitMu) after any concurrently in-flight Commit send under the same lock has already completed and released it.
